Subject: Post-demo: payment method gating & procurement checklist for AuroraMed

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the time, Lara. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can map the right commercial path for AuroraMed.

What I heard on the call (summary):
- You're excited about the latency/cost profile for clinical note generation at scale.
- Procurement & AP have specific vendor onboarding gates and a preferred payment path.
- Pilot budget is small but expected to scale into a committed annual contract if results look good.

Questions / asks (to confirm):
1) PO threshold: what annual or per-vendor spend requires a formal PO vs. card?
2) Vendor docs: do you need a completed vendor form + W9 before purchase, or is that only for PO setups?
3) Marketplace: is purchasing via a cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP marketplace) acceptable to avoid the vendor setup?
4) Billing cadence: do you require monthly invoices, net-30, or a different cadence for software services?

Attached: Redwood pricing grid (pilot vs committed) and our standard vendor onboarding checklist.

Proposed next step: I can loop in our finance ops lead (Marissa) and your AP contact for a 30-min call to nail down the path (PO vs card vs marketplace). Are you available next Thursday afternoon PT?

Thanks — happy to be flexible based on what AP needs.

--
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference — inference for production

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Grid_2026.pdf, Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist_AuroraMed.docx
From: Lara Mendez <lara.mendez@auroramed.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: AuroraMed AP <ap@auroramed.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:18:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: payment method gating & procurement checklist for AuroraMed

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from AP side below so we can decide the right route. Forwarding to AP for any clarifications.

- PO threshold: For any vendor where we expect > $25,000 / year we require a PO and vendor setup in our ERP. For pilots under $5,000 we typically allow a department corporate card. Anything between $5k–$25k is handled case-by-case; prefer PO if the vendor will be long-term.
- Vendor docs: We do require a completed vendor form plus W9 for vendor setup. For card charges we can delay vendor setup until the PO/contract stage, but we'll still need the W9 for accounting.
- Marketplace: AuroraMed limits marketplace purchases — we only allow a few vetted platforms (mainly our cloud infra marketplace). If Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace and the SKU matches what we need, that is often the fastest route because it avoids vendor onboarding.
- Billing cadence: Net-30 preferred. Monthly invoices are fine; we can handle quarterly if that's how you price committed capacity.

I attached the vendor onboarding checklist we use internally — it lists required fields and typical turnaround.

If Marissa can join the call, we can decide on PO vs. card and confirm the timeline for vendor setup.

Best,
Lara Mendez
Director, Clinical Operations
AuroraMed

Thanks, Lara — this is really helpful. TL;DR — two pragmatic paths:

1) Fast pilot (under $5k): card payment, one-off, we can issue a single invoice and provide deliverables. No immediate vendor setup required; you can run the pilot this month.
2) Production / committed capacity (>$25k/year): PO + vendor onboarding in your ERP, net-30 invoices. That path takes ~2–4 weeks for vendor setup once the vendor form + W9 are submitted.

Questions for AP (for the call):
- If we ran a pilot on card and it scales, can you convert to a PO quickly and backdate any necessary records?
- Is a DocuSign MSA required before PO issuance or can PO be issued while MSA is under signature?

Attachments I’m sharing now: updated pricing grid and a redlined MSA mask we use for pilots (for legal to fast-track).

Proposed call: Wed 14 Jan 2026 at 11:00 AM PT — 30 minutes with Lara + Marcus Lee from AP + Marissa and Karthik from our side. LMK if that works; otherwise propose two times.

Thanks — happy to coordinate the logistics.

Aditya / Lara — Marcus Lee here (AP). Thanks for pulling this together. A few quick notes and next steps: 

- Confirmed: PO required for > $25k/year. We can accept card for pilots under $5k.
- Vendor setup timeline: once we receive the completed vendor form + W9, typical turnaround is 7–10 business days.
- DocuSign / MSA: We do not require the fully executed MSA before issuing a PO, but we do require a signed SOW or a confirmed purchase request to create the PO.
- Marketplace: We can do marketplace purchases only if the product is available on our approved marketplace list. Please share the marketplace listing link if applicable.

Next steps I can own: I attached a blank vendor form and my contact details — please return the completed form with W9. I'll queue the vendor setup and expedite where possible. Also confirm whether you want to run the pilot on card (quickest) or start the PO process.

Available for a short call Wed 14 Jan 11:00 AM PT, as Aditya suggested.

Marcus Lee
